title: Perfect projection formula on arbitrary small ringed sites
statement:
Let $u:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with sheaves of commutative rings and structural map $u^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use their ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the canonical derived adjunction $L=Lu^*\dashv R=Ru_*$ and K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let $E\in D(R_X)$ and let $P\in D(R_Y)$ be perfect, meaning that locally on the target site it is represented by a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free $R_Y$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Then the canonical projection morphism
$$\pi_{u,E,P}:RE\otimes^L_{R_Y}P\longrightarrow R(E\otimes^L_{R_X}LP),$$
defined as the adjunct of $L(RE\otimes^LP)\xrightarrow{\sim}LRE\otimes^LLP\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_E\otimes1}E\otimes^LLP$, is an isomorphism. No boundedness of $E$, global bound on the local perfect representatives, exactness of module pullback, cartesianness, or geometric finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For each ordinary slice at U use [lem-sbc-projection-mate-slice-presentation]. This gives exact shift-compatible local functors and a natural mate, with the exact equation comparing it to restriction of the global projection. Derive invertibility of the global mate at the ring directly from the unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], cancelling the invertible mapped tensor-unitor. Restriction carries the single degree-zero global ring to the single degree-zero slice ring, via mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor and the sectionwise identity on restricted ring modules. The mate equation and naturality then prove invertibility of the local mate at the slice ring.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; projection morphism immediately preceding the lemma

proof.text: Apply the existing proved NatTrans.isoLocus API: the isomorphism locus of a shift-compatible natural transformation between exact triangulated functors is a triangulated object property, closed under isomorphisms and retracts. Finite products of the degree-zero ring lie in this locus because the degree-zero single functor preserves finite products. The splittings in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] exhibit each term of a strict-perfect representative as a retract of such a finite product, including rank zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-complex-triangulated-devissage] to deduce invertibility at Q(T) for every bounded strict-perfect representative T. Naturality transports it to the restricted coefficient. This uses the proved source module WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Generators, not a new triangle induction.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; projection morphism immediately preceding the lemma

proof.text: For a perfect object choose its global representative K. For each site object W choose its covering sieve of strict-perfect local representatives. Index a single covering family by all triples (W,U,f) with f:U -> W in that sieve, using U as the corresponding domain. It covers every W because each original covering sieve is contained in its sieve of domains. At each member, the quasi-isomorphism from the strict-perfect complex and the representative isomorphism give r_U(P) isomorphic to Q(T). Steps 1 and 2, followed by cancellation of the target comparison, make restriction of the specified global projection mate invertible.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; projection morphism immediately preceding the lemma

proof.text: Prove local detection of arbitrary derived arrows by replacing their target with a K-injective complex using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Essential surjectivity of Q gives a complex for the source, and the K-injective Hom comparison lifts the derived arrow to a chain map g. The natural exact-restriction factorization identifies Q(r_U g) with restriction of Q(g), hence each r_U g is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact restriction commutes with short-complex homology. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the underlying sheaf map of each H^n(g), then reflect isomorphisms back to modules. Thus g is a quasi-isomorphism, so Q(g) is invertible. Cancel the two representative isomorphisms to obtain invertibility of the original derived arrow. Apply this to the global projection mate and the covering family of step 3.
